summary.headline: Redington Q4 FY26 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR 33,269 crore and adjusted PAT hit a record INR 467 crore (1.4% margin), before a INR 75.2 crore Arena impairment.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was Redington's best quarter on both revenue and profit, led by India (revenue +50%, PAT +41%) and strong TSG and PC demand. Middle East was hit by the West Asia conflict from 28 February 2026, with March weak and supply, insurance and receivable issues. FY26 revenue was INR 119,347 crore (+20%) with adjusted PAT +17% and PAT margin 1.3%. Management guided to a soft Q1 FY27 and a dividend of INR 6 per share (30% payout), while conserving cash for inorganic growth and larger large-deal working capital.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue +50% and PAT +41% in Q4; growth across all business units, with up-country expansion +45% and data-centre deals with neo-cloud operators.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Revenue +19% YoY, about 33% of top line in Q4; driven by premium smartphones and direct-to-retail in India, while Middle East premium demand was constrained.

segments.name: Endpoint Solutions Group (PCs)
segments.commentary: Revenue +28% YoY, about 30% of top line; boosted by component-shortage pull-forward, price increases and large deals of nearly INR 500 crore; 41% of India commercial AI PC revenue from >40 TOPS models.

segments.name: Technology Solutions Group (TSG)
segments.commentary: Revenue +34% YoY, about 19% of top line; record revenue as data centre, networking and server/storage all grew, with large deals above INR 1,100 crore and some deals shifted from Q3 to Q4.

segments.name: Software Solutions Group (SSG)
segments.commentary: Revenue +31% YoY, 17% of top line in Q4 (17% for FY26 vs 15% in FY25); cloud and software growing above 30%, security growing slower and needs catch-up; target gross margin 5.5-6%.

segments.name: Arena (Turkey, Lira business)
segments.commentary: Q4 loss of INR 44 crore (Redington share INR 22 crore, including exit costs on Lira business); exiting Lira phone and mix businesses by FY26 end, focus shifting to USD-based IT and cloud; Arena book value about $8 million.

segments.name: Middle East and Africa clusters
segments.commentary: Middle East is 30-35% of business; Q4 UAE +6% (FY +22%), KSA -12% (FY +5%), GCCL +51% (FY +33%), Africa +26% (FY +13%).

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 expected to be soft, with India demand strong but Middle East softness likely in Q1 and partly Q2; management said the trajectory is similar to March, neither worse nor better.
Middle East recovery expected to follow resolution of the West Asia crisis; Saudi Arabia expected to stay soft until IT priorities are clear.
Opex to stay elevated for 1-2 years as capability-building investment continues; AR provisions and war-related insurance and freight costs expected to normalise.
EBITDA outside Arena guided at about 2.2%-2.4%, subject to large-deal mix; ROCE to stay above 18% (currently near 20%).
Arena losses expected to continue into FY27 at a reduced level, with a real turnaround in the subsequent year; Turkey demand expected to soften further.
Large deals were about INR 1,600 crore+ in Q4 and about INR 2,500 crore for FY26; management expects this to keep rising in H1 FY27, with more working capital needed.
capex_capacity: No formal capex or capacity figures disclosed; management is exploring inorganic opportunities, particularly in cloud and security professional services.
AI Exchange marketplace launched mid-March with 200+ AI agents from ISVs; AI revenue expected to start during FY27.
Cloud Quarks platform 2.0 rolled out in Q4 with digital lifecycle analytics and automated subscription renewals.
India data centre market at 1.5 GW, expected to reach 7.5 GW in a few years; management is building a data-centre plan covering hardware, power, cooling and co-location.
demand_pricing: Component shortages (PCs, smartphones, GPUs) and expected price increases drove Q4 PC demand; ASP-led growth expected to be significant, with unit growth marginal.
Management does not expect COVID-style margin and working-capital gains; gross margin to be maintained, but working capital may rise on credit and stock-up needs.
Middle East war caused insurance withdrawal on 7 days' notice, higher retention, and supply-chain and logistics disruption; alternate warehousing and imports via Europe and Mumbai used.
Large deals will be lower margin than the core business; management will hold to ROCE and working-capital discipline rather than margin percentage.

Software: management sees no visible subscription softening from AI models so far, but expects AI-native security tools to be a watch item; Microsoft Copilot cited as an example of OEM tie-ups extending to other LLM providers.

qa_highlights.question: How should FY27 be framed, with India growth vs rest of world recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: India expected to keep growing with a soft Q1; Middle East and Africa strong in H1 once the crisis eases; management said it is not sure when the crisis will end.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable and inventory provisioning split by India and RoW?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory provision about 3 bps for FY26 vs 5-6 bps long-term average; AR provisions higher due to one-offs in Saudi and India government receivables; AR may normalise, with partial recovery possible.

qa_highlights.question: Opex, factoring and employee cost trends, and dividend rationale?
qa_highlights.answer: Factoring fell sharply (Arena: INR 22 crore in Q4 FY25, INR 18 crore in Q3, INR 2 crore in Q4 FY26); employee cost up on capability investment and rupee at 94 vs 88. Dividend kept low to conserve cash for inorganic and large-deal needs.

qa_highlights.question: Large-deal guidance and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Large deals were about INR 2,500 crore for FY26, with Q4 at INR 1,600+ crore; margins much lower than core, but ROCE will not be compromised.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East inventory risk and insurance cover?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurers withdrew war cover on 7 days' notice; Redington added cover elsewhere and moved stock across warehouses, now said to have adequate coverage with some higher retention in the interim.

qa_highlights.question: SSG gross margin and profitability outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: SSG gross margin tracked at about 5.5%, with an intended 5.5-6% range; professional services expected to lift margin; resell pressure to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Reconciling INR 467 crore, INR 287 crore and INR 391 crore profit figures?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 467 crore excludes the Arena impairment exceptional item; INR 287 crore is PAT before minority; INR 391 crore is after minority, including the impairment share.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: duration unknown; Middle East is 30-35% of business and March was weak; Saudi softness expected to persist.
Arena (Turkey): continued losses in FY27; remaining book exposure about $8 million and a $12 million receivable with slower collections; further impairment possible if market value falls.
Opex and interest cost rise: elevated employee and technology spend for 1-2 years, plus higher interest costs from factoring and working capital.
Working capital and receivables: AR provisions higher; working capital may rise with large deals and stock-building.
Supply and pricing: component shortage duration (12-18 months) and when price increases end are unclear; pull-forward demand could reverse in 2-3 quarters.
AI disruption to security and SaaS subscription models is unproven but under watch; security growth lags cloud and software.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India and the overall year, but cautious on Middle East and Turkey; management repeatedly flagged uncertainty about the West Asia crisis and conserved cash for growth. Some answers were defensive, particularly on the profit reconciliation and Arena balance-sheet exposure.
key_quotes: This has been our best quarter so far from both revenue and profit perspective.
Our performance was driven by resilience and defined by discipline.
But no compromise on return on capital employed.
So that elevated opex for next couple of quarters, maybe 1 or 2 years would continue is our expectation.
